title: build save <id> --confirm <token> writes jitso/builds/<id>.yaml with status approved and every other byte of the draft, removes the draft, and the build is then listed and valid
source: intended: docs/decisions.md D7 and B3-18/B3-19 (a draft becomes a build only with the owner's OK: a terminal, or the token of the content he read; the guard denies the agent)
intent: INTENDED behavior (defect N-15, drafts; docs/decisions.md D7). The token printed by the refusal binds the owner's OK to the content he read: `jitso build save <id> --confirm <token>` with that token writes `jitso/builds/<id>.yaml`, which is the draft bytes with the `status` scalar `draft` replaced by `approved` and nothing else changed, removes `.jitso/drafts/<id>.yaml`, shows the file with `+ ` prefixes and prints `saved <id>: jitso/builds/<id>.yaml (status approved); the draft is removed`, exit 0. The saved build is a repo build: `build list` shows it and `build validate <id>` says ok. The oracle has no `build save` (the runner maps only `build list`): it answers `unknown command` on stderr with exit 2 and prints nothing on stdout, so every expectation that needs the `+ ` lines, the token text or the written file FAILS on it.
